title: Triage playbook: dependency fast-path + SIEM bridge
body:
Purpose
This working doc describes a proposed fast-path triage and evidence-export flow for dependency vulnerabilities that integrates RBAC v2, the audit-log schema, automated evidence collection, and SIEM export requirements. Objective is to shorten time-to-fix for high-impact package issues while preserving auditability and forensics.

Intended audience
- Security engineers and triage oncall
- SREs and infra owners
- Release and product engineering leads
- SOC / SIEM team

High-level summary
1) Fast-path eligibility: low-risk-to-deploy, high-likelihood-easy-fix dependency issues (e.g., patchable OSS library with upstream patch available and no API break noted) will be routed through an expedited workflow.
2) RBAC v2 gating: only users in the "vuln-triage-fastpath" and "release-owner" roles may approve fast-path fixes; approvals must be recorded per audit schema fields.
3) Evidence automation: scanner outputs (CycloneDX/SBOM-derived), CI build artifacts, and package lock diffs are attached automatically to the remediation ticket. Evidence is staged, hashed, and mapped to the audit_log schema before SIEM export.
4) SIEM bridge: a compact SIEM export record is emitted for every triage decision (accept/reject/deferral) and for patch deployment events.

Detailed triage flow (fast-path)
- Step 0: Scanner detection. Tools: dependency-scanner (oss-dep-scan) runs nightly and on PR. Sample raw line: "oss-dep-scan|pkg:golang/github.com/foo/bar@v1.2.3|CVE-2027-12345|8.1|fix: 1.2.4"
- Step 1: Auto-enrich. Evidence collector queries SBOM, checks changelog for fix, verifies a passing upstream test vector if available, and resolves affected services from asset registry.
- Step 2: Fast-path rule engine. Rules to mark eligible: severity >=7.0 OR exploit maturity >=2 AND upstream patch available within last 90 days AND affected services have automated canary pipeline.
- Step 3: Create triage ticket with prepopulated remediation template and attached evidence bundle (SBOM snippet, lockfile diff, upstream PR link, sample failing test if present). Ticket field sample: "fastpath_reason: upstream_patch_available; evidence_hash: sha256:..."
- Step 4: RBAC v2 approval. Only users in the group can approve. Approval action writes an audit_log entry per schema below. Approver must select deployment window or "emergency" option.
- Step 5: CI/CD patch rollout. Pipelines have a required canary step and mandatory rollback timeout. On completion, automation notes deployment status back to ticket and triggers SIEM export event.

RBAC v2 mapping for triage roles (proposal)
- Role: vuln-triage-reader -> read access to vuln tickets and evidence artifacts (no approve)
- Role: vuln-triage-fastpath -> create and approve fast-path tickets; limited to non-prod deployments if flagged
- Role: release-owner -> can approve fast-path to prod deployments; must have MFA enforced and manager attestation in attributes
- Role: vuln-admin -> manage rules, escalate, and perform mass remediation
Notes: Roles are represented as attributes in RBAC v2 engine with resource scoping (org/team/service). Audit entries must include role attribute snapshot at time of action.

Audit log schema (compact mapping for triage)
We will reuse the canonical audit schema but include a compact vuln-specific payload that SIEM expects. Fields (flattened):
- event_id (uuid)
- timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
- actor (email)
- actor_role (string)
- action (triage.create|triage.approve|triage.defer|deploy.start|deploy.finish|evidence.attach)
- vuln_id (CVE or internal id)
- package (purl)
- severity_cvss (numeric string)
- fastpath_reason (string or empty)
- evidence_hashes (comma-separated sha256)
- ticket_id (JIRA- key)
- service_scope (comma-separated service ids)
- deployment_window (string or empty)
- decision_ttl (minutes, string)
- outcome (accepted|rejected|deferred|rolled-back)
- raw_scanner_feed (short fingerprint; not full raw to limit SIEM storage)
Implementation note: these fields are strings to simplify SIEM ingestion. The audit-log writer transforms internal types to strings and drops fields >8k chars.

Evidence automation mapping and retention
- Evidence types: sbom_snippet, lockfile_diff, upstream_patch_link, ci_artifact_sha, test_vector (if any), binary_sig (if available)
- Each evidence file is hashed and stored in evidence-bucket with path: evidence/{ticket_id}/{sha256}. Metadata saved in triage DB and a compact manifest attached to ticket.
- Retention policy: 1 year for low/medium, 7 years for high/critical incidents to support compliance requests.
- Access: read via RBAC v2 checks; deletion only via vuln-admin or via retention job.

SIEM export: event types and cadence
- triage.decision (on triage complete) -> emitted immediately (low volume)
- deployment.lifecycle (start/finish/rollback) -> emitted on pipeline transitions
- evidence.attach (when large evidence bundles are created) -> only emits manifest record, not full files
- metrics.shipped (periodic aggregate of unresolved counts and patch SLA compliance) -> daily
Payload size and throttling: SIEM bridge will truncate long arrays and include only first-3 evidence_hashes. Older events beyond 90 days archived to cold store; SIEM gets pointers.

Patch SLA matrix (proposed)
- Critical (CVSS >=9 OR active exploit) -> 24 hours to mitigation action (patch, mitigation, or exception documented)
- High (7-8.9) -> 7 days to mitigation action
- Medium (4-6.9) -> 30 days to mitigation action
- Low (<4) -> 90 days or documented acceptance
Mitigation action means: patch applied in canary OR documented compensating control + evidence attached. Exceptions require manager + security approval and create an audit_log entry.

Remediation tracking and ticket lifecycle
- Ticket states: detected -> triaged -> fastpath_approved OR scheduled_work -> in_progress -> canary_passed -> prod_rolled -> closed -> postmortem_needed (if rollback or incident)
- Each transition must emit audit_log event; tickets missing any audit log entry for a transition are flagged for manual review.
- Rollback handling: rollout failures auto-create a rollback incident ticket and attach rollback evidence (pipeline logs, system snapshots).

Dependency dedupe heuristics (why duplicates happen)
- Same CVE across multiple package managers (e.g., transitive JS deps vs compiled binary) -> dedupe by vuln fingerprint plus service scope intersection
- Different versions of same package -> group under a single parent ticket with per-version subtasks when the remediation path is shared
- Rules: prefer single canonical ticket per service-scope-week to avoid alert fatigue; exceptions for criticals.

Operational metrics to track (dashboard inputs)
- Mean time to remediation action (per severity)
- Fast-path acceptance rate and time-to-approval
- Evidence attachment success rate (percentage of tickets where evidence collector succeeded)
- SIEM export success and dropped events by reason
- RBAC approval audit latency (time between action and audit log write)

Open questions / TODOs
- How to represent multi-approver policies in RBAC v2 for cross-org services? (Priya to propose attribute-based approach)
- Hashing and encryption: should evidence hashes be HMACed with a per-tenant key before SIEM export? Security to weigh in.
- Archive pointer format: confirm with SIEM whether they prefer object-time or ticket-time pointers.
- Integrate runtime scanner (container image vulns) with same fast-path rules — Do we allow same fast-path for runtime images? (SRE feedback needed)
- Prototype metrics: Diego to wire up a Prometheus exporter for fastpath flows by 2027-05-15.

Appendix: example SIEM event (flattened CSV-like payload)
"event_id=8f7b9e2c-... ,timestamp=2027-04-12T03:22:11Z,actor=aisha.kapoor@redwood.ai,actor_role=vuln-triage-fastpath,action=triage.approve,vuln_id=CVE-2027-12345,package=pkg:cargo/serde@1.0.104,severity_cvss=8.2,fastpath_reason=upstream_patch_available,evidence_hashes=sha256:aaa...,sha256:bbb...,ticket_id=JIRA-SEC-3124,service_scope=payments,gateway,deployment_window=emergency-2027-04-12,outcome=accepted,raw_scanner_feed=fingerprint-ef23"

Notes to reviewers
- This is a working draft; the goal is to lock the RBAC mapping and audit fields in Q2 and iterate on evidence retention in Q3.
- Please add comments inline in Confluence-SEC-TRIAGE-7421 and link any related PRs.

Change log
- 2027-04-12: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2027-04-20: added RBAC v2 role table and SIEM field truncation rules (Priya)
- 2027-05-03: updated retention policy and open questions (Diego)
